summary: A status list covering RFCs 2400 through 2499, with each RFC's author, date, title and abstract. It notes which ones are on the standards track. It is an informational index rather than a protocol specification.

eli5.summary: This is like a table of contents for a shelf of one hundred RFC booklets, listing who wrote each one, when, and what it is about.

subtitle: A reference index and summary of 100 RFCs published between 2400 and 2499.

tldr.problem: A researcher or implementer needs a quick overview of what 100 consecutive RFCs are about, their authors, dates, and track status.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC is a status list providing the title, author, date, and abstract for each RFC from 2400 through 2499, with notes on which ones are on the standards track.
tldr.outcome: A browsable reference document that helps readers find relevant RFCs from this period without reading each one individually.

today: RFC 2499 is an Informational RFC that serves as an index and finding aid for RFCs 2400-2499. It has been superseded by later RFC summary documents covering newer ranges, but it remains a historical reference for understanding what was published during this period of Internet standardization.

sections.title: About This Document
sections.content:
RFC 2499 is a slightly annotated list of the 100 RFCs from RFC 2400 through RFC 2499, published in July 1999. It provides a status report on these RFCs, listing each one's author, publication date, and title.

The RFC notes that many of these RFCs are Proposed Standards, Draft Standards, or Standards on the standards track, though the status of RFCs may change during standards processing. Readers are directed to the latest version of "Internet Official Protocol Standards" for current status information.
sections.eli5: This is a list of 100 documents about internet stuff from around 1998-1999. Each one has a name, author, and short explanation of what it does.

sections.title: Coverage and Topics
sections.content:
The 100 RFCs in this range cover a broad spectrum of Internet protocols and applications. Topics include:

  • IPv6 and related protocols (address allocation, multicast, packet format, link layer support)
  • Security and cryptography (ESP, AH, IPsec, encryption algorithms, X.509 certificates, OpenPGP)
  • Routing protocols and multicast (OSPF extensions, RIP version 2, multicast benchmarking)
  • Transport and application protocols (TCP enhancements, FTP extensions, SMTP security)
  • MIB definitions and network management (DS0/DS1/DS3 interfaces, IPv6 management objects)
  • Quality of service and differentiated services architecture
  • Multimedia and real-time protocols (RTP payload formats for video and audio)
  • Messaging and calendaring (iCalendar, MIME handling, email extensions)
  • Simulation models and network analysis
sections.eli5: These documents are about sending information on the internet in new ways, keeping it secret, organizing how networks work, and measuring how well things run.

sections.title: Standards Track Status
sections.content:
Within this range, many RFCs are marked as being on the standards track (Proposed, Draft, or Full Standard), while others are Informational, Experimental, or Best Current Practice documents.

According to the document, the reader should consult the latest "Internet Official Protocol Standards" document for the current status of each RFC, as status can change during IETF standards processing. Standards track RFCs represent protocols being actively considered for standardization, while Informational RFCs document research, simulation results, or requirements analysis.
sections.eli5: Some documents here are official internet standards, some are still being worked on, and some are just explaining something that's interesting but not a standard yet.

sections.title: Notable RFCs in This Range
sections.content:
Some significant RFCs in this range include: RFC 2400 (Official Protocol Standards), RFC 2401-2408 (IPsec and key management suite), RFC 2460 (IPv6 Specification), RFC 2461-2462 (IPv6 Neighbor Discovery and Autoconfiguration), RFC 2475 (Differentiated Services Architecture), RFC 2487 (SMTP over TLS), and RFC 2490 (IP Multicast with RSVP simulation model).

Earlier in the range, RFC 2419 covers PPP DES encryption, and various RFCs define MIB objects for managing network interfaces. Later RFCs cover IPv6 deployment, security protocols, and real-time media formats.
sections.eli5: This range includes the big document about IPv6 (the new version of the internet address system), ways to keep internet traffic secret, and ways to measure network quality.

references.text: Internet Architecture Board, "Internet Official Protocol Standards", RFC 2400, September 1998.
